 Police inquiry into election-day contacts with Netanyahu’s office remains frozen 
 Police inquiry into election-day contacts with Netanyahu’s office remains frozen
 The attorney general and state attorney will meet again to discuss the Ra’am cash envelopes affair. A decision on whether to open a criminal investigation is pending
 i24NEWS 2 min read 2 min read  ■  Israel 
 election 
 Netanyahu 
 Israel elections 2026 
 Google News Follow us Follow Benjamin Netanyahu at the Knesset, in Jerusalem, on November 17, 2026 Chaim Goldberg/Flash90 
 An internal police review of contacts between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office and senior police officials around election day will remain on hold after a meeting Wednesday evening between Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara and the state attorney, i24NEWS learns.
 The meeting centered on the Ra’am cash envelopes affair, an election bribery case. Grinzaig reported that Police Commissioner Dani Levi would be instructed to keep the internal review led by his deputy on hold until further notice.
 Separately, the Lahav 433 police unit has begun examining the conduct of the Prime Minister’s Office. On the eve of the election, Netanyahu’s chief of staff contacted the police commissioner’s office to raise suspicions of foreign interference in the vote.
 Israeli media Channel 12 reported that an intelligence source in the election bribery case works in the Prime Minister’s Office and supplied investigators with key details that turned out to be false. Police are examining whether the source knowingly gave them false information or made a mistake.
 New report claims Netanyahu’s office allegedly gave police false intel regarding election meddling The Attorney General’s Office said Baharav-Miara had asked Levi to pause the internal review while legal officials examine how the information was passed to police and decide how the matter should be investigated.
